body:
## 🗒️ Description

### What
Wires the deterministic citation verifier added in #259 into `review()`, so citations are checked against the PR diff before a review is submitted.

- `src/webhook_agent/review/grounding.py` (from #259) is now called from `tools/github_tools.py::review()`.
- New flag `STRICT_REVIEW_GROUNDING`, defaulting to `"0"` in `constants.py`.
- When the investigation gate already iterates `pr.get_files()`, that same pass records the patch text, so grounding adds no call. When the gate skips that iteration (prefetched `deterministic_changed_files`, or the gate disabled), `_collect_pr_patches()` makes one `pr.get_files()` call instead. The review path makes at most one such call; never two.

> **Correction:** an earlier revision of this description claimed the prefetch path adds no API call. That was inverted -- the prefetch path is exactly where the single call happens. The bot reviews on this PR carried the original wording forward as a RESOLVED risk without re-checking it, so this note corrects the record.

### Behaviour
- Every `critical_issues` / `minor_suggestions` / `verified_invariants` citation is verified against the diff.
- **All** grounding issues are logged with severity and code, whether or not enforcement is on.
- **Enforcement is off by default.** With `STRICT_REVIEW_GROUNDING=1`, only `hard` issues are appended to `invalid_findings` and returned to the model as a self-correction error.
- `soft` issues (a line the diff does not display, a changed file with no patch text) are logged but **never** enforced, because their false-positive rate is unmeasured.
- When no patch text is available at all, the check logs `Grounding check skipped ...` and treats citations as unverified rather than valid. A check that cannot distinguish "no" from "could not tell" is worse than no check, so that distinction is explicit and has its own test.

### Why the flag defaults off
`MAX_AUDITOR_LLM_CALLS=6` plus a 3-comments-per-minute limiter means a verifier with a false-positive bug can make the reviewer reject itself into exhaustion or never post. Measure first, then harden — same pattern as `ALLOW_AUTOMATED_MUTATIONS`.

---

## 🧪 Testing

Five integration tests in `tests/unit/review/test_review_tool_validation.py`, going through `review()` itself rather than the pure verifier:

| Test | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `test_grounding_does_not_reject_when_not_strict` | a hard failure is logged, review still submits |
| `test_grounding_rejects_hard_failure_when_strict` | strict mode rejects, and `_submit_formal_review` is not called |
| `test_grounding_soft_issues_never_reject_even_when_strict` | a line outside the diff does not reject |
| `test_grounding_skips_and_logs_when_patch_text_is_unavailable` | cannot-verify is logged and does not reject |
| `test_grounding_rejects_unciteable_verified_invariant_when_strict` | the APPROVE path is grounded too |

**CI is green:** `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy --show-error-codes`, and the full suite (447 passed, 1 skipped, 2 xfailed -- the two xfails are the known defects recorded in #259). The five new grounding tests are included.

They were not run locally, because this change was authored in an environment with no installable interpreter. That cost four CI cycles to converge: two formatting, one blank-line, and one test-context bug where the mandatory investigation gate rejected four of the five tests before they reached the code under test.

```bash
./scripts/ruff-all.sh
uv run pytest tests/unit/review/test_review_tool_validation.py -q
uv run pytest --tb=short -q
```

---

## 📦 Configuration Impact

- [x] Update README.md environment variables (N/A - no env var table exists in README)
- [x] Update pyproject.toml if adding dependencies (N/A - zero new dependencies)
- [x] Run `uv sync` after dependency changes (N/A)

---

## 🔒 Security Checklist

- [x] No secrets or credentials hardcoded
- [x] HMAC signature verification logic unchanged
- [x] Authentication/authorization behavior preserved
- [x] Webhook payload handling validated
- [x] New behaviour is fail-closed on enforcement (off by default) and fail-open on verification capability (cannot-verify is reported, not silently passed)

---

## 🔗 Related

- Depends on #259 (merged)
- Implements Phase 2.2 of `docs/plans/reviewer_hardening_plan.md`
- Phase 3 is the next step: require the reviewer to quote the source line it cites, which is the only fix for the right-file/wrong-line blind spot documented in #259

+def _collect_pr_patches(pr: Any) -> dict[str, str | None]:
+    """Collect ``{filename: patch}`` for the grounding check. Never raises.
+
+    Returns an empty mapping when no patch text is available, so the caller can tell
+    "cannot verify" apart from "verified nothing" instead of silently passing.
+    """
+    try:
+        return {
+            str(file.filename): getattr(file, "patch", None)
+            for file in pr.get_files()
+            if getattr(file, "filename", None)
+        }
+    except Exception as err:
+        logger.debug("Could not collect PR patches for the grounding check: %s", err)
+        return {}
+
+
+def _citation_finding(kind: Kind, item: Any) -> Finding:
+    """Adapt one parsed review finding into a grounding citation finding."""
+    # Imported locally: a module-level import would pull webhook_agent.tools.diff_tools
+    # in while webhook_agent.tools.__init__ is still executing.
+    from webhook_agent.review.grounding import Finding
+
+    evidence = getattr(item, "evidence", None) or getattr(item, "description", None) or ""
+    return Finding(
+        kind=kind,
+        path=getattr(item, "path", None) or "",
+        line=getattr(item, "line", None),
+        evidence=str(evidence),
+    )
+
+
+def _grounding_findings(review_obj: Any) -> list[Finding]:
+    """Adapt every cited finding in a parsed review response into citation findings."""
+    findings: list[Finding] = []
+    for item in getattr(review_obj, "critical_issues", None) or []:
+        findings.append(_citation_finding(kind="critical", item=item))
+    for item in getattr(review_obj, "minor_suggestions", None) or []:
+        findings.append(_citation_finding(kind="suggestion", item=item))
+    for item in getattr(review_obj, "verified_invariants", None) or []:
+        findings.append(_citation_finding(kind="invariant", item=item))
+    return findings
+
+
+def strict_grounding_enabled() -> bool:
+    """Return True when ungrounded citations should reject a review, not merely log."""
+    return os.environ.get("STRICT_REVIEW_GROUNDING", DEFAULT_STRICT_REVIEW_GROUNDING) in (
+        "1",
+        "true",
+        "True",
+    )
+

+        # Deterministic citation grounding: check every cited path/line against the diff.
+        # Always logged; only enforced when STRICT_REVIEW_GROUNDING is set, because a
+        # verifier with a false-positive bug can otherwise reject reviews into exhaustion.
+        from webhook_agent.review.grounding import (
+            diff_text_from_patches,
+            hard_reasons,
+            verify_citations,

+
+        grounding_patches = patches or _collect_pr_patches(pr)
+        if not grounding_patches:
+            logger.warning(
+                "Grounding check skipped for %s#%s: no patch text available to verify "
+                "citations against. Treating citations as unverified, not as valid.",
+                repo_name,
+                pr_number,

+        else:
+            grounding_issues = verify_citations(

+            if grounding_issues:

+                    repo_name,
+                    pr_number,

+            if strict_grounding_enabled():
+                invalid_findings.extend(hard_reasons(grounding_issues))

         if invalid_findings:

## 🛡️ Code Review: `APPROVE`

### 1. Executive Summary

This pull request successfully implements Phase 2.2 of the reviewer hardening plan by wiring the deterministic citation verifier (`webhook_agent.review.grounding`) directly into the `review()` tool execution path within `src/webhook_agent/tools/github_tools.py`. By introducing the default-off configuration flag `STRICT_REVIEW_GROUNDING` (`DEFAULT_STRICT_REVIEW_GROUNDING = "0"`), the system securely measures and logs citation accuracy without risking reviewer exhaustion or deadlocks due to false-positive enforcement bugs.

Architecturally, the patch collection logic elegantly integrates with the existing investigation-gate loop to avoid redundant GitHub API calls on the primary code path, while maintaining a robust fallback via `_collect_pr_patches()` that handles API errors gracefully and distinguishes genuine verification failures from unverified scenarios. Furthermore, comprehensive test coverage in `tests/unit/review/test_review_tool_validation.py` thoroughly validates all operational permutations—including non-strict warning behavior, strict hard-failure rejections, soft-issue immunity, unavailable patch text handling, and invariant citation validation.

title: feat(review): enforce citation grounding behind a default-off flag
